module: Make and maintain the deployment decision

lesson.title: Decide whether a fundamental-rights assessment is needed
lesson.summary: Test the FRIA trigger and reuse applicable data-protection evidence without a waiver.

prerequisites.reason: The obligation is imposed on specified deployers.
The Annex III route and point matter

blocks: A **fundamental-rights impact assessment**, or FRIA, examines the effects of a deployment on people’s fundamental rights before deploying the specified system. Article 27 concerns Article 6(2) Annex III systems, except Annex III point 2 critical infrastructure.

Within that route, the actor/use triggers are bodies governed by public law, private entities providing public services, and deployers of Annex III 5(b)/(c) systems: creditworthiness/credit scoring and life/health-insurance risk/pricing. A purely private recruitment employer is not automatically covered solely because recruitment is high-risk.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Articles 26(9), 27(1)–(5); GDPR Article 35 / LED Article 27 as separate applicability lookups
EDPB: data protection impact assessment and its separate likely-high-risk trigger

blocks: **FRIA content** includes the actual process and intended use, time/frequency, affected people/groups, specific likely harms informed by provider information, implementation of human oversight, and responses if risks materialise, including internal governance and complaint mechanisms.
A provider’s generic test report does not by itself assess a public-service deployer’s actual process, people or complaints arrangements. Link evidence to each assessment element.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Articles 26(9), 27(1)–(5); GDPR Article 35 / LED Article 27 as separate applicability lookups
EDPB: data protection impact assessment and its separate likely-high-risk trigger

blocks: The duty applies to first use. Similar cases may rely on previous assessments or provider assessments, but changed or outdated elements require updating. After assessment, notify the market-surveillance authority with the filled template; the Article 46(1) exceptional route may exempt notification.

Article 27 directs the AI Office to develop a questionnaire/template, including an automated tool. Verify the actual available version before treating a form as official. The course does not assert that a usable template has been published.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Articles 26(9), 27(1)–(5); GDPR Article 35 / LED Article 27 as separate applicability lookups
EDPB: data protection impact assessment and its separate likely-high-risk trigger

blocks: A **data protection impact assessment**, or DPIA, is the separate assessment required under data-protection law when its conditions apply. GDPR Article 35’s general trigger is processing likely to cause high risk to individuals’ rights/freedoms. The Law Enforcement Directive has its own Article 27 route.

Article 26(9) requires using provider information for a DPIA where applicable. High-risk AI classification alone does not decide every DPIA condition. Check processing facts, the relevant data law and authority guidance/lists; specialist triggers are lookup gates here.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Articles 26(9), 27(1)–(5); GDPR Article 35 / LED Article 27 as separate applicability lookups
EDPB: data protection impact assessment and its separate likely-high-risk trigger

blocks: **FRIA/DPIA reuse** under 27(4) lets a deployer cross-reference relevant sections or include relevant material where the DPIA already fulfils FRIA obligations. It does not waive the remaining FRIA elements or notification.

Case variant: a public-law body uses the stipulated Annex III recruitment system. Its DPIA covers personal-data risks but lacks complaint/governance arrangements and deployment frequency. Reuse relevant content and complete the missing applicable FRIA elements.

questions.prompt: A purely private recruitment employer, providing no public service, uses Annex III 4(a). Is Article 27 automatically triggered solely by high-risk status?

options.blocks: No; test the specified actor/use trigger
options.reason: High-risk status alone is insufficient for this provision.

options.blocks: Yes; every high-risk deployer has a FRIA duty
options.reason: The provision has limited triggers and a point 2 exclusion.

options.blocks: No public-law body can ever trigger it
options.reason: Public-law actors are expressly within the stated route.
